title: Easy Chicken Recipes
excerpt: Find easy chicken recipes for weeknights and Sunday supper—baked chicken, ground chicken, pasta, casseroles, wings, and slow cooker dinners, all gathered in one cozy guide.
featuredImageAlt: Easy chicken recipes featuring roast chicken, baked chicken, pasta, and family dinner sides
contentHtml:
When you need supper that feels like home, chicken recipes are the first place most of us look. A good chicken dinner can be as simple as a weeknight sheet pan or as special as a golden Sunday roast. This guide gathers Grandma Recipe’s best easy chicken recipes by cooking style—baked and roasted, skillet and ground chicken, pasta nights, cozy casseroles, wings, and slow cooker meals—so you can pick a path and cook with confidence.

Use this page as your starting point. Each section below points to tested recipes with clear steps, familiar ingredients, and that comforting, from-scratch flavor we love around the family table.

How to Use This Chicken Recipes Guide

Start with the cut you have, then choose the method that matches your evening:

  • Short on time? Try baked chicken breast, air fryer chicken, or a sheet-pan supper.
  • Want something cozy? Open a casserole, pot pie soup, dumplings, or a crockpot chicken dinner.
  • Feeding a pasta crowd? Jump to the chicken pasta cluster for creamy, skillet, and baked noodles.
  • Cooking for game night? Wings, tenders, and hot chicken belong on that table.

If you are new to roasting a whole bird, begin with How to Roast a Chicken. For a reliable boneless dinner, start with Juicy Baked Chicken Breast.

Choose Your Chicken Cut

Matching the cut to the recipe is half the battle.

  • Boneless chicken breast cooks quickly and stays mild. Best for baking, slicing over rice, and creamy skillet sauces. See Juicy Baked Chicken Breast.
  • Chicken thighs stay juicy and forgiving. Bone-in or boneless both shine in the oven—try Chicken Thighs and Oven-Baked Boneless Chicken Thighs.
  • Whole chicken is Sunday supper in one pan. Learn the method in How to Roast a Chicken, or keep it easy with One Pan Roasted Chicken.
  • Ground chicken makes tender meatballs, skillet meals, and lighter comfort food. Start with Skillet Chicken Meatballs.
  • Wings and tenders bring crispy edges and big flavor—Crispy Buffalo Chicken Wings, Crispy Honey Garlic Wings, Homemade Chicken Tenders, and Breaded Chicken Strips.

Chicken Cooking Basics

A few kitchen habits keep chicken recipes juicy instead of dry:

  • Pat the meat dry before seasoning so you get better browning.
  • Season under and over the skin on bone-in pieces for flavor that reaches the meat.
  • Cook to a safe internal temperature of 165°F in the thickest part. An instant-read thermometer takes the guesswork away.
  • Rest briefly after cooking so the juices settle before you slice.
  • Use the pan juices—a spoonful over the meat tastes like home.

For oven nights, baked chicken and roasted chicken are your friends. For hands-off evenings, slow cooker chicken and rice or white chicken chili can simmer while you set the table.

Baked and Roasted Chicken Recipes

Oven chicken recipes are the backbone of an easy weeknight or a quiet Sunday. High heat for color, steady heat for tenderness, and simple seasoning are all you need.

  • How to Roast a Chicken — crisp skin, tender meat, and savory pan juices.
  • Juicy Baked Chicken Breast — a dependable boneless dinner with garlic and herbs.
  • Oven-Baked Boneless Chicken Thighs — juicy oven thighs with less fuss than a whole bird.
  • One Pan Roasted Chicken — chicken and vegetables share one roasting pan.
  • Hawaiian Chicken Sheet Pan Dinner — a bright sheet-pan dinner with sweet-savory flavor.
  • Monterey Chicken and Smothered Chicken — saucy baked chicken for when you want comfort on a plate.
  • French Onion Chicken and Easy Aloha Chicken — weeknight favorites with big flavor from pantry ingredients.
  • Peri Peri Chicken — a bolder roast-style chicken when the table wants a little heat.

These baked chicken recipes pair beautifully with rice, mashed potatoes, green beans, or a simple salad. If you are building a meal around leftovers, slice roast chicken into wraps, soups, or next-day pasta.

Ground Chicken Recipes

Ground chicken is lighter than beef but still hearty when you season it well and keep the mixture moist. It shines in skillet dinners, meatballs, and family-friendly pasta nights.

  • Skillet Chicken Meatballs — cozy skillet meatballs in tomato sauce over noodles.
  • Crack Chicken Sliders — party-ready chicken sliders for busy evenings.

Tips for ground chicken recipes: do not overwork the meat, add a binder like breadcrumbs or egg when shaping, and brown in a hot skillet before simmering in sauce so you keep savory flavor.

Chicken Pasta Recipes

Chicken and pasta belong together on busy nights. Creamy sauces, baked casseroles, and skillet noodles all earn a place in this cluster.

  • Marry Me Chicken Pasta — creamy, sun-dried tomato comfort in one skillet.
  • Tuscan Chicken Pasta — garlic, greens, and tender chicken with pasta.
  • Crack Chicken Penne — rich, cheesy penne the whole table finishes.
  • Crockpot Chicken Alfredo Pasta — hands-off Alfredo for crockpot evenings.
  • Chicken Baked Ziti — baked ziti with chicken for potluck-style dinners.
  • Cajun Chicken and Sausage Pasta — spicy sausage-and-chicken pasta with Cajun warmth.
  • Lemon Chicken Orzo — bright lemon chicken with tender orzo.
  • Keto Chicken Parmesan — a lighter chicken Parmesan-style plate when you want fewer carbs.

Serve chicken pasta recipes with garlic bread and a crisp salad. Leftovers reheat gently with a splash of broth or milk to loosen the sauce.

Chicken Casserole Recipes

Casseroles are Grandma’s answer to “what’s for dinner” when the oven can do the work. Creamy sauces, rice or crackers, and a golden top make these chicken recipes feel like a hug.

  • Chicken Broccoli Rice Casserole — classic chicken, broccoli, and rice in one dish.
  • Ritz Cracker Chicken Casserole — buttery cracker topping over tender chicken.
  • Doritos Chicken Casserole — a fun, crunchy family casserole night.
  • Chicken Pot Pie Hand Pies — chicken pot pie flavor in hand-held pies.

Make-ahead tip: assemble most chicken casseroles earlier in the day, refrigerate, then bake until bubbling and golden before supper.

Wings and Crispy Chicken

When you want crunch and sauce, this cluster is the place. Oven and air fryer methods keep things simpler than deep frying while still delivering that satisfying bite.

  • Crispy Buffalo Chicken Wings — classic tangy heat.
  • Crispy Honey Garlic Wings — sticky-sweet wings with garlic.
  • Nashville Hot Chicken — fiery hot chicken for spice lovers.
  • Air Fryer Parmesan Crusted Chicken — crisp Parmesan crust without heating the whole kitchen.
  • Homemade Chicken Tenders and Breaded Chicken Strips — kid-friendly crispy chicken for dipping.

Set out ranch or blue cheese, celery, and a simple slaw. Crispy chicken recipes also tuck into sandwiches and wraps the next day.

Crockpot and Slow Cooker Chicken

Slow cooker chicken recipes turn tough evenings into gentle ones. Add the ingredients in the morning, and come home to a kitchen that smells like supper already started.

  • Slow Cooker Chicken and Rice — tender chicken and rice in one pot.
  • Slow Cooker Chicken Stroganoff — creamy slow cooker comfort.
  • White Chicken Chili Crockpot — white chicken chili for chilly nights.
  • Crockpot Chicken Alfredo Pasta — pasta night without standing at the stove.
  • Homemade Chicken and Dumplings — homemade chicken and dumplings when you want a bowl of comfort.
  • Chicken Pot Pie Soup — pot pie flavor in a spoonable soup.

For best texture, keep chicken pieces similar in size, and shred or slice only after the meat is fully cooked and tender.

Sheet Pan, Skillet, and Wrap Night

Not every chicken dinner needs a long bake. Sheet pans, skillets, and wraps keep prep light and cleanup kinder.

  • Hawaiian Chicken Sheet Pan Dinner — colorful sheet-pan supper.
  • One Pan Roasted Chicken — roast chicken and vegetables together.
  • Skillet Chicken Meatballs — skillet meatballs for pasta night.
  • Chicken Shawarma Wrap — wrap-ready chicken with bold seasoning.
  • Homemade Chicken Ramen — a cozy bowl when noodles sound better than rice.

What to Serve with Chicken

Round out chicken recipes with sides that feel familiar:

  • Fluffy rice, mashed potatoes, or buttered noodles
  • Green beans, roasted carrots, or a simple garden salad
  • Warm bread, rolls, or garlic toast for saucy plates
  • A light dessert if Sunday supper needs a sweet finish

For rice sides that never fail, you can also explore our rice guides—chicken and rice is a classic pairing for a reason.

Make Ahead, Storage, and Leftovers

  • Refrigerate cooked chicken within 2 hours in shallow containers. Use within 3 to 4 days.
  • Freeze cooled portions in airtight containers for up to 2 to 3 months.
  • Reheat until steaming hot. Add a splash of broth to sliced breast meat so it stays moist.
  • Leftover ideas: chicken salad, quesadillas, soup starters, pasta tosses, and grain bowls.

FAQs About Chicken Recipes

How do I keep baked chicken breast from drying out?

Do not overbake, season well, and rest a few minutes before slicing. Our Juicy Baked Chicken Breast walks through a juicy oven method step by step.

Is dark meat better for beginners?

Often yes. Thighs stay moist even if they cook a little longer, which makes Oven-Baked Boneless Chicken Thighs a forgiving place to start.

Can I swap chicken thighs for breasts?

Yes in many skillet and casserole recipes. Expect a slightly richer flavor and adjust cook time so the thickest piece reaches 165°F.

What is the safest internal temperature for chicken?

Cook chicken to 165°F in the thickest part. For a whole roast, check the thigh without touching the bone—see How to Roast a Chicken.

Which chicken recipe should I make first?

If you want a classic Sunday feeling, make How to Roast a Chicken. For a weeknight, choose Juicy Baked Chicken Breast, Hawaiian Chicken Sheet Pan Dinner, or Marry Me Chicken Pasta.

Final Thoughts

Good chicken recipes do not need complicated tricks—just the right cut, honest seasoning, and a method that fits your night. Bookmark this guide, pick a cluster, and cook one recipe at a time. Before long you will have a little rotation of family favorites ready for weeknights and Sundays alike.
